title: The voter-facing document has the weakest independence guarantee in the Executive chain
content:
**Side A — code review is strict.** Spell code requires reviewer separation enforced across teams and rotated per cycle, with the validator mandated to assume the answering party is acting maliciously.

**Side B — document review is not.** The Executive Document — the artifact voters actually read to decide — is reviewed within the same team, with author/reviewer separation stated only "as a general rule."

The asymmetry is backwards relative to the threat. Code defects are caught by hashes, diffs, simulation and independent reconstruction; **framing and omission errors in the voter-facing description are caught by none of those.** A Spell that does exactly what its code says, described in a way that leads voters to a different conclusion, passes every technical control in the chain.

This is not a contradiction in the strict sense — both provisions can hold simultaneously — but it is a live tension between the Atlas's stated adversarial posture and where it spends its review budget.

**To resolve:** consider whether the Executive Document warrants the same cross-team separation the code path already mandates.
description: Spell code requires hard per-cycle cross-team reviewer separation, while the Executive Document that voters actually read is reviewed intra-team with author/reviewer separation only as a general rule.
